newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Sayansk aluminium sees steady output.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Sayansk aluminium sees steady output.

text.p: Russia's Sayansk aluminium plant SALU.RUO maintained output despite a strike earlier this month by workers at a power station supplying the facility, Sayansk president Oleg Deripaska said on Thursday.

He told Reuters in a telephone interview that Sayansk had secured steady supplies of electricity from the Sayano-Shushenskoy hydroelectric power station after making a five billion rouble advance payment for October supplies.
The payment covers Sayansk's electricity needs for seven to 10 days.
Deripaska said Sayansk output was not affected by a 40-person hunger strike at the power station from September 3 to September 11.
He said Sayansky Alyuminievy Zavod (SAAZ) would work out a direct payment arrangement with the power station by 1997.
The agreement would bypass the local utility, Khakasenergo, which Sayansk currently pays for its electricity supplies.

"I expect a long-term agreement, with the price of electricity tied to the price of aluminium on the London Metal Exchange, by the end of November," Deripaska said. "We and Sayano want to establish a direct relationship."
Electricity costs are a major factor in aluminium output.
